title: 盖梯尔案例：碰巧对的真信念
titleEn: Gettier: Justified True Belief, Right by Luck
lead: 你有理由相信、命题也恰好为真——但真是运气使然。这还算「知道」吗？
leadEn: You are justified, the proposition is true—yet only by luck. Is that knowledge?

points.v: 史密斯有充分证据相信「老板的车是福特」，据此推出「有人有一辆福特」。而老板的车其实不是福特，但同事琼斯恰好有一辆福特——结论为真。
points.vEn: Smith has good evidence that his boss owns a Ford, so he infers 'someone in the office owns a Ford'. The boss's car is not a Ford, but Jones happens to own one—the conclusion is true.

points.v: 知识＝确证的真信念这条两千年的分析被一个反例击穿：确证、真、信念俱备，却没人会说自己「知道」。
points.vEn: A two-millennium analysis—knowledge as justified true belief—falls to one counterexample: justification, truth and belief are all present, yet nobody would claim to know.

points.v: 增加「无缺陷论证」条件、因果论（信念须由事实引起）、可靠论（由可靠过程产生）、德性认识论（出于智识德性）。
points.vEn: Add a no-false-lemmas condition; causal theories (belief caused by the fact); reliabilism (produced by a reliable process); virtue epistemology (from intellectual competence).

points.v: 「认知运气」似乎不可完全消除；有些学者因此放弃给知识下定义，转而研究知识的实践功能。
points.vEn: Epistemic luck seems impossible to purge entirely; some therefore abandon the definitional project and study knowledge's practical role instead.

sources.label: 盖梯尔《被确证的真信念是知识吗》
sources.labelEn: Gettier, Is Justified True Belief Knowledge?

title: 缸中之脑
lead: 若你的经验全由机器输入，你能凭内在证据判断自己不是缸中之脑吗？
leadEn: If all your experience were machine-fed, could internal evidence show you are not a brain in a vat?

points.v: 邪恶科学家维持离体大脑并输入与真实世界无法区分的信号；「我有手」在这两种情形下体验相同。
points.vEn: An evil scientist keeps a detached brain fed with signals indistinguishable from a real world; 'I have hands' feels the same either way.

points.v: 它是笛卡尔恶魔与庄子梦蝶的当代版本，把怀疑从感官扩展到整个外部世界的存在。
points.vEn: It is Descartes' demon and Zhuangzi's dream in modern dress, extending doubt from the senses to the existence of an external world.

points.v: 用因果指称论论证「我是缸中之脑」这一句子若为真即不可被真地说出——语义外在论对怀疑论的釜底抽薪（其效力争议至今）。
points.vEn: With causal reference theory he argues the sentence 'I am a brain in a vat' cannot be truly uttered if true—semantic externalist sabotage of scepticism, still disputed.

points.v: 把「确证是否需要世界-independent 的立足点」摆上台面，是知识论与科学方法论的共同暗题。
points.vEn: It forces the question whether justification needs a footing independent of the world—the shared hidden problem of epistemology and philosophy of science.

sources.label: 普特南《理性、真理与历史》第一章
sources.labelEn: Putnam, Reason, Truth and History, ch. 1

title: 庄周梦蝶
lead: 不知周之梦为胡蝶与，胡蝶之梦为周与——提问的重心不在真假，而在「谁在判」。
leadEn: Unknown whether Zhuang Zhou dreamed he was a butterfly, or the butterfly dreams he is Zhou—the stress falls not on truth but on who is judging.

points.v: 庄周梦为蝴蝶，栩栩然自适；醒来则「周与蝴蝶则必有分矣」，此之谓物化。
points.vEn: Zhou dreams he is a butterfly, entirely at ease; waking, there must be a division between the two—this is called the transformation of things.

points.v: 笛卡尔用恶魔怀疑以求第一确定；庄子不给「确定的我」这个出口，把怀疑写成一种安顿。
points.vEn: Descartes doubts by a demon to reach first certainty; Zhuangzi refuses the exit of a certain 'I' and writes doubt as a kind of ease.

points.v: 瓦解「判准自证」的幻觉：任何验证都已在某一立场之内，故《齐物论》转向「两行」而非裁判。
points.vEn: It undermines the dream of self-validating criteria—every test already sits within some stance, so the Qiwulun turns to letting both courses run rather than adjudicating.

points.v: 与不可判别经验等价物（underdetermination）、梦境认识论、乃至身份与叙事自我的当代讨论同族。
points.vEn: Kin to underdetermination, the epistemology of dreams, and current debates on identity and the narrative self.

sources.label: 《庄子·齐物论》末章

title: 忒修斯之船
lead: 木板逐根更换后仍是同一艘船？那么用旧木板重组的那艘呢？
leadEn: Is the ship still the same after every plank is replaced? And what of the one rebuilt from the old planks?

points.v: 雅典人保留忒修斯的船，逐根换新木料；霍布斯追加：若集齐旧料另组一船，谁才是「那艘」？
points.vEn: The Athenians keep the ship, replacing planks one by one; Hobbes adds: if the old timber is reassembled into a second ship, which is 'the' one?

points.v: 物质连续性、形式或结构连续性、功能与历史链条、四维主义（各时间部分是不同整体）。
points.vEn: Material continuity, formal or structural continuity, functional-historical chain, four-dimensionalism (temporal parts as different wholes).

points.v: 同一性关系要求传递且唯一，而「逐渐更换」与「另组一物」各自看似成立，两者不能同时为真。
points.vEn: Identity must be transitive and one-one, yet gradual replacement and reassembly each look correct, and both cannot be.

points.v: 细胞代谢、记忆中断、人格分裂（Parfit 的分裂案例）把船的问题变成「我是否还是我」的问题。
points.vEn: Cellular metabolism, gaps in memory and fission cases (Parfit) turn the ship question into whether I am still I.

sources.label: 普鲁塔克《忒修斯传》
洛克《人类理解论》同一段

title: 分裂传送器（Parfit 的分裂）
lead: 如果把一个人的心理状态完整复制到两个人身上，「谁是我」这个问题还有事实答案吗？
leadEn: If one person's psychology is copied onto two, is there still a fact about which one is me?

points.v: 分裂实验：大脑半球分别植入两个身体，两者都醒来、都自称原主，且各自与原来心理连续。
points.vEn: Fission: each hemisphere is transplanted into a different body; both wake, both claim to be the original, each psychologically continuous with him.

points.v: 同一性是一一对应关系，故二者至多一个是原主；但心理连续性与连接度（Relation R）两者皆备——而「这才重要」。
points.vEn: Identity is one-one, so at most one is him; yet both enjoy psychological continuity and connectedness (Relation R)—and that is what matters.

points.v: 自我并非额外的「第三种实体」；对「我的未来」的特殊关切被解释为关系结构，而不是同一性事实。
points.vEn: There is no further separate entity that is the self; special concern for my future is read as a relational structure, not an identity fact.

points.v: 批评者认为取消自我使道德责任与承诺失去主体；支持者看到对佛教无我与休谟束理论的现代印证。
points.vEn: Critics say dissolving the self leaves responsibility and promise without a subject; supporters see a modern confirmation of non-self and Hume's bundle.

sources.label: 帕菲特《理与人》第十、十二部分
sources.labelEn: Parfit, Reasons and Persons, parts 10 and 12

title: 中文房间
lead: 只会按规则搬运符号的人，能让屋里「懂中文」吗？强人工智能的质疑由此而来。
leadEn: Can a man who merely shuffles symbols by rule make the room understand Chinese? The case against strong AI.

points.v: 不懂中文的人在房内据规则册处理中文符号，外面的中文者得到完美答案。
points.vEn: A speaker of no Chinese inside a room processes Chinese symbols per a rulebook, giving fluent answers to outsiders.

points.v: 语法（句法操作）不足以产生语义（理解）；因此纯计算的程序本身不构成心智。
points.vEn: Syntax alone is not sufficient for semantics; hence a purely computational program does not by itself constitute a mind.

points.v: 理解或许属于整个系统而非房中人——塞尔否认此点，争论聚焦在「何处安放理解」。
points.vEn: Perhaps the whole system understands, not the man inside—Searle denies it, and the dispute centres on where understanding may be located.

points.v: 在大模型时代被反复引用：行为流畅是否等于理解，成为经验可测而非纯概念的问题（可解释性、基准与语言测试）。
points.vEn: Repeatedly cited in the era of large models: whether behavioural fluency equals understanding has become an empirically testable question (interpretability, benchmarks, linguistic probes).

sources.label: 塞尔《心灵、大脑与科学》

title: 玛丽的房间
lead: 黑白房间里学尽红色所有物理知识的科学家，第一次走出房间看见红色时，学到了新东西吗？
leadEn: The scientist who learned every physical fact about red inside a black-and-white room—does she learn something new on seeing red?

points.v: 杰克逊的设想：玛丽拥有全部物理信息但从未有颜色经验。
points.vEn: Jackson's setup: Mary knows every physical fact about colour yet has never had a colour experience.

points.v: 若她出房时说出「原来红色是这样」，则存在物理描述未穷尽的事实——论证物理主义不完整。
points.vEn: If on leaving she says 'so this is what red is like', then facts exceed physical description—and physicalism is incomplete.

points.v: 能力假说（她获得的是 know-how 而非新命题知识）、代表主义（经验内容由表征状态说明）、现象判断的错觉论。
points.vEn: The ability hypothesis (she gains know-how, not new propositional knowledge), representationalism, and illusory accounts of phenomenal judgement.

points.v: 「解释间隙」究竟在世界上还是在概念上——这是感受质与难问题争论的真正战场。
points.vEn: Whether the explanatory gap lies in the world or in our concepts—that is the real battleground of qualia and the hard problem.

sources.label: 杰克逊《感受质》

title: 哲学僵尸
lead: 物理上与你不差分毫、却没有任何「像什么」的体验——这样的存在可设想吗？
leadEn: Physically indistinguishable from you yet with nothing it is like to be it—is such a being conceivable?

points.v: 查尔莫斯的僵尸：行为、语言、神经活动全都一致，唯缺现象意识。
points.vEn: Chalmers' zombie: behaviour, speech and neural activity identical, phenomenal consciousness absent.

points.v: 可设想 → 逻辑可能 → 物理事实不蕴含意识事实 → 物理主义为假（意识是附加事实）。
points.vEn: Conceivability → logical possibility → physical facts do not entail phenomenal facts → physicalism is false.

points.v: 物理主义者否认这种可设想性真正支持形而上可能（类型错位、二次信念论）；异象论者干脆否认僵尸概念前后一致。
points.vEn: Physicalists deny that conceivability evidences metaphysical possibility (misdescription, higher-order views); illusionists deny the concept is coherent at all.

points.v: 它把「难问题」精确定义为解释的缺口，使关于意识的科学议程必须回答：解释到什么程度算完成。
points.vEn: It pins the hard problem as an explanatory gap, forcing consciousness science to say what would count as a completed explanation.

sources.label: 查尔莫斯《有意识的心灵》

title: 孪生地球
lead: 另一个地球上看起来是水、化学式却是 XYZ 的液体——两地人说「水」时，想法相同吗？
leadEn: On Twin Earth a liquid looks like water but is XYZ. When both say 'water', do they think the same thought?

points.v: 普特南设想一颗行星，其「水」的微观结构为 XYZ，与 H₂O 在一切可感性质上相同。
points.vEn: Putnam imagines a planet whose 'water' has microstructure XYZ, indistinguishable sensorily from H₂O.

points.v: 两地的「水」指称不同自然类，故含义不全在头脑之中——「语义外在论」。
points.vEn: Their 'water' refers to different natural kinds, so meaning is not wholly in the head—semantic externalism.

points.v: 孪生双胞胎的区分、严格指示词与自然种类术语的先天偶然论，共同重塑语言哲学与心灵哲学。
points.vEn: Twin distinctions, rigid designators and the contingent-a-priori status of natural-kind terms reshaped philosophy of language and mind.

points.v: 若含义依赖环境，自我知识与「一阶权威」须被重新解释；内在论者以双重内容（窄内容/宽内容）折中。
points.vEn: If meaning depends on environment, self-knowledge and first-person authority must be re-described; internalists compromise with narrow and wide content.

sources.label: 普特南《意义的意义》

title: 电车难题
lead: 拉杆救五杀一，还是不动手任五死？差别在结果，还是在你的作为？
leadEn: Pull the switch to save five and kill one, or refrain and let five die—does the difference lie in outcomes or in your doing?

points.v: 失控电车将轧死五人；岔道只有一人。变体「天桥」：推下一人可阻车。多数人对二者判断不同。
points.vEn: A runaway tram will kill five; the siding holds one. Variant: push a man off a footbridge to stop it. Most people judge the two cases differently.

points.v: 后果主义看总效用；义务论看不可侵犯性与手段—目的；双重效果论与「doing/allowing」区分承担中间立场。
points.vEn: Consequentialism counts aggregate welfare; deontology looks at inviolability and treating persons as means; double effect and the doing/allowing distinction stake out middle ground.

points.v: 神经影像与损伤研究显示，个人化伤害触发情绪—社会认知系统，非个人化情形更多依赖代价—收益计算（Greene 的双过程模型）。
points.vEn: Imaging and lesion work suggest personal harm engages emotional and social-cognitive systems while impersonal cases lean on cost-benefit computation (Greene's dual-process model).

points.v: 自动系统的路径选择使难题从思想实验变为政策问题；批评者指出以「拉杆」建模会遮蔽责任分配与制度设计。
points.vEn: Automated systems turn the thought experiment into policy; critics argue that switch-style framing obscures liability and institutional design.

sources.label: 富特《道德中的道德困境》
sources.labelEn: Foot, The Problem of Abortion and the Doctrine of Double Effect

sources.label: 汤姆森《电车问题》

title: 经验机器
lead: 机器能给你一切你想要的体验，且你不知自己在机器中——你会接入吗？若不愿，快乐就不是唯一的好。
leadEn: A machine can give every experience you want, and you would not know you were plugged in. Would you plug in? If not, pleasure is not the only good.

points.v: 诺齐克的机器可定制终身体验，接入后不能中途反悔了解真相。
points.vEn: Nozick's machine offers a lifetime of custom experience; once plugged in you cannot later learn the truth.

points.v: 反驳快乐主义的福利论：我们也在乎「真的在做」「成为某种人」「与实在接触」。
points.vEn: Against hedonistic welfare theory: we also care about actually doing something, being a certain kind of person, and contact with reality.

points.v: 后续研究（包括 De Neys 等的「虚拟享乐主义」实验）显示相当比例受试愿意接入，且久后直觉减弱——直觉是否可靠证据被重新讨论。
points.vEn: Later studies (including 'wireheading experiments') find many willing to plug in, with the effect growing over time—reopening whether intuitions are trustworthy evidence.

points.v: 意义理论、体验机器在娱乐与社交平台上的现实版本（沉浸、算法推荐）都构成同一追问的当代形态。
points.vEn: Theories of meaning, and real-world analogues in immersive media and recommendation algorithms, are contemporary forms of the same question.

sources.label: 诺齐克《哲学解释》

title: 纽康姆悖论
lead: 两个盒子与一位几乎全对的预言者：两个都拿，还是只拿不透明的那个？两种推理原则给出相反答案。
leadEn: Two boxes and a near-perfect predictor: take both, or only the opaque one? Two decision principles answer oppositely.

points.v: 透明盒内有 1000 元；不透明盒由预言者依对你选择的预测放入一百万或空。预言者准确率极高。
points.vEn: The transparent box holds 1,000; the predictor placed a million in the opaque box, or nothing, according to its prediction of your choice, and is highly accurate.

points.v: 占优原则说两个都拿（无论预言者放什么，多一个盒子总不坏）；期望效用计算说只拿不透明盒（拿一个者几乎总得百万）。
points.vEn: Dominance says take both—whatever was placed, an extra box cannot hurt. Expected-utility reasoning on the correlation says take only the opaque one.

points.v: 因果决策论与证据决策论之争；也牵动自由意志（预言与选择能否共存）与理性自我的时间结构。
points.vEn: Causal versus evidential decision theory; it also touches free will (can prediction and choice coexist) and the temporal structure of the rational self.

points.v: 在包含 AI 与算法预测的决策场景中被重新引用；一箱派与两箱派至今未分出胜负。
points.vEn: Re-cited where AI and algorithmic prediction shape decisions; one-boxers and two-boxers remain at an impasse.

sources.label: 诺齐克《纽康姆问题》
sources.labelEn: Nozick, Newcomb's Problem and Two Principles of Choice

title: 法兰克福案例
lead: 黑手党随时会替你按下按钮——但你按了自己的。你没得选，可你仍应负责吗？
leadEn: A mafia would have forced your hand had you hesitated—but you chose it yourself. With no alternative available, are you still responsible?

points.v: 琼斯决定捐款；布莱克监控其神经，若琼斯不起此意便强行让他起意。实际中布莱克从未介入。
points.vEn: Jones decides to donate; Black monitors his neurology and would force the decision had Jones wavered. As it happens, Black never intervenes.

points.v: 反驳「他可能别作选择」原则（PAP）：此处无其他可能性，琼斯却看似仍应负责。
points.vEn: Against the Principle of Alternate Possibilities: Jones could not have done otherwise, yet seems responsible.

points.v: 微光论者（flicker）否认案例中缺少其他可能性（仅缺其可及性）；兼容论者与不兼容论者各取所需；「追踪序列」变体继续争论。
points.vEn: Flicker defenders deny the absence of alternatives (only their accessibility is missing); compatibilists and incompatibilists each claim the case; tracking-sequence variants keep the argument alive.

points.v: 对胁迫、成瘾、算法助推与自动系统的责任归属性讨论提供共同模板——关键在「机制是否属于你」而非「是否有后门」。
points.vEn: It supplies a shared template for coercion, addiction, nudging and automated systems—what matters is whether the mechanism is yours, not whether a back door exists.

sources.label: 法兰克福《替代可能性原则》
sources.labelEn: Frankfurt, Alternate Possibilities and Moral Responsibility

title: 原初状态（选择程序的实验）
lead: 把立约者剥去一切特殊信息，让他们为自己立法——他们会选什么原则？
leadEn: Strip contractors of all particular information and let them legislate for themselves—which principles would they choose?

points.v: 参与者不知自己的阶级、天赋、种族、性别、善观念与世代，只知社会、经济与心理的一般事实。
points.vEn: Parties know no facts about their class, talents, race, sex, conception of the good or generation—only general social, economic and psychological facts.

points.v: 罗尔斯认为在极大风险厌恶下，理性者会选平等基本自由与差别原则，而非平均效用——因为后者可能牺牲最不利者。
points.vEn: With strong risk-aversion, rational parties pick equal basic liberties and the difference principle rather than average utility, which could sacrifice the least advantaged.

points.v: 哈桑伊指出无知之幕下应取「期望」而非「最小最大」；社群主义质疑「无负荷的自我」；女性主义与全球正义问：幕布为何止于国界与家庭。
points.vEn: Harsanyi urges expected rather than maximin choice under the veil; communitarians reject the unencumbered self; feminists and global theorists ask why the veil stops at borders and the household.

points.v: 正义被表述为「选择程序的公平」：不问何谓正确分配，而问何种程序设计能生成可辩护的结果（反思平衡的一部分）。
points.vEn: Justice becomes fairness of procedure: not what counts as a right distribution, but which procedure yields defensible outcomes—part of reflective equilibrium.

sources.label: 罗尔斯《正义论》§24–§30

title: 内格尔的蝙蝠：作为一只蝙蝠是什么感觉
titleEn: Nagel's Bat: What Is It Like to Be a Bat?
lead: 你可以穷尽蝙蝠的一切神经生理，却仍不知道「用声呐听世界」究竟是怎样的体验。
leadEn: You may exhaust the bat's neurophysiology and still not know what it is like to hear the world by sonar.

points.v: 蝙蝠靠回声定位「看」世界，其主观样式远超人类想象，我们只能凭自身感官去猜。
points.vEn: Bats perceive by echolocation; their subjective style far exceeds human imagination, and we can only guess from our own senses.

points.v: 一旦承认「有某种成为蝙蝠的样子」，就说明存在无法被客观描述穷尽的事实。
points.vEn: Once you grant there is 'something it is like' to be a bat, some facts escape any complete objective description.

points.v: 直指还原论与功能主义：第三人称的物理／功能说明，似乎总漏掉第一人称的感受性质。
points.vEn: It targets reductive and functionalist programmes: third-person physical/functional accounts seem to leave out first-person feel.

points.v: 「解释的鸿沟」由此得名；有人诉诸新神秘主义，有人仍寄望未来的科学将其跨越。
points.vEn: The 'explanatory gap' is named here; some invoke a new mysterianism, others still trust future science to close it.

sources.label: 内格尔《作为一只蝙蝠是什么感觉》
sources.labelEn: Nagel, What Is It Like to Be a Bat?

title: 罗素的火鸡：归纳的信任
titleEn: Russell's Turkey: The Faith of Induction
lead: 一只火鸡观察到「主人每天来喂食」，一日日越发确证——直到圣诞前夜，规律第一次背叛了它。
leadEn: A turkey notes 'the farmer comes to feed me' day after day, ever more confirmed—until Christmas Eve, when the pattern first betrays it.

points.v: 火鸡从大量一致的经验中归纳出「主人来＝有食物」这一规律，并深信不疑。
points.vEn: From many uniform observations the turkey induces 'farmer comes → food' and trusts it completely.

points.v: 再多正面例证，也不能在逻辑上保证未来必重演过去的秩序。
points.vEn: No amount of positive instances logically guarantees the future will repeat the past order.

points.v: 它是休谟归纳问题的寓言：「太阳明天照常升起」建立在习惯而非证明之上。
points.vEn: It is Hume's problem of induction in fable: 'the sun will rise tomorrow' rests on custom, not proof.

points.v: 波普尔以可证伪取代归纳确证；也有人以自然齐一性或最佳解释推理为其辩护。
points.vEn: Popper swaps inductive confirmation for falsifiability; others defend the uniformity of nature or inference to the best explanation.

sources.label: 罗素《哲学问题》中的归纳寓言
sources.labelEn: Russell, The Problems of Philosophy (the inductive bird)

title: 洛克：王子与鞋匠的同一
titleEn: Locke: The Prince and the Cobbler
lead: 若王子的记忆搬进鞋匠的身体，换上宫廷衣裳的是「同一个人」，还是仅仅同一具躯壳？
leadEn: If a prince's memory moved into a cobbler's body, is it the same person in courtly clothes, or merely the same body?

points.v: 洛克设想意识（连同记忆）随王子转移进一具陌生的躯体。
points.vEn: Locke imagines consciousness—together with memory—transferring with the prince into an unfamiliar body.

points.v: 他由此区分「人（一团物质）」与「人格（自我）」：人格的同一系于记忆的连续，而非物质相同。
points.vEn: He splits 'man (a lump of matter)' from 'person (a self)': personal identity tracks continuity of memory, not sameness of substance.

points.v: 里德批评记忆链会传递断裂（少年—军官—老者），使洛克式记忆论陷入矛盾。
points.vEn: Reid objects that the memory chain breaks transitivity (boy–officer–hoary general), landing Locke's view in contradiction.

points.v: 它开启了心理连续论，也逼出帕菲特「同一并非要紧之事」的后续追问。
points.vEn: It opens psychological-continuity views and provokes Parfit's sequel that identity is not what matters.

sources.label: 洛克《人类理解论》「论同一与差异」

title: 威廉斯：吉姆与二十名人质
lead: 若吉姆不开枪，二十人将被杀；若他亲手杀一人，其余十九得救。功利的算法干净利落，却像漏掉了什么。
leadEn: If Jim does not shoot, twenty die; if he kills one with his own hand, nineteen are saved. The utilitarian calculus is clean—yet something seems left out.

points.v: 残暴队长允诺：吉姆若亲手处决一名人质，余者即刻获释，否则二十人全被杀。
points.vEn: A brutal captain offers this: if Jim executes one hostage himself the rest go free at once, else all twenty are killed.

points.v: 简单功利主义叫吉姆开枪（净多救十九），却无视他的完整人格与自身的计划、信念。
points.vEn: Simple utilitarianism bids him shoot (nineteen net saved) but ignores his integrity and his own projects and commitments.

points.v: 威廉斯以此批评功利计算把人当作中性管道，抹去行动者自己的道德账目。
points.vEn: Williams charges that the calculus treats persons as neutral conduits, erasing the agent's own moral ledger.

points.v: 后果主义者反驳：拒开亦使吉姆双手沾上二十条命——「不作为」并非无辜。
points.vEn: Consequentialists reply: refusing also stains Jim—with twenty deaths; 'doing nothing' is not innocent.

sources.label: 夏与威廉斯《功利主义：赞成与反对》
sources.labelEn: Smart & Williams, Utilitarianism: For and Against
